```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# traceroute-internal.sh
# Usage:
#   ./traceroute-internal.sh               # uses hostnames in HOSTS below
#   ./traceroute-internal.sh host1 host2   # uses args as targets
# Env:
#   TR_BIN=traceroute|tracepath|tracert...  # override binary
#   OUTDIR=./traceroute-results            # output directory
#   MAX_HOPS=30
#   WAIT_SEC=2
#   QUERIES=1
#   MODE=udp|icmp|tcp
#   TCP_PORT=443                           # when MODE=tcp

HOSTS=(
  "dc01.internal"
  "files.internal"
  "git.internal"
  "db01.internal"
  "app01.internal"
)

TR_BIN="${TR_BIN:-traceroute}"
OUTDIR="${OUTDIR:-./traceroute-results}"
MAX_HOPS="${MAX_HOPS:-30}"
WAIT_SEC="${WAIT_SEC:-2}"
QUERIES="${QUERIES:-1}"
MODE="${MODE:-udp}"          # udp (default), icmp (-I), tcp (-T)
TCP_PORT="${TCP_PORT:-443}"  # only used when MODE=tcp

timestamp="$(date -u +'%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')"
mkdir -p "$OUTDIR"

log() { printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +'%F %T UTC')" "$*" >&2; }

if ! command -v "$TR_BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "ERROR: '$TR_BIN' not found. Install traceroute (or set TR_BIN=tracepath)."
  exit 127
fi

# Prefer args if provided; otherwise use HOSTS array
targets=("$@")
if [[ ${#targets[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  targets=("${HOSTS[@]}")
fi

# Build options for common traceroute implementations (Linux/macOS)
opts=(-n -m "$MAX_HOPS" -w "$WAIT_SEC" -q "$QUERIES")
case "$MODE" in
  udp) : ;;
  icmp) opts+=(-I) ;;
  tcp)  opts+=(-T -p "$TCP_PORT") ;;
  *)
    log "ERROR: MODE must be udp|icmp|tcp (got: $MODE)"
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

for host in "${targets[@]}"; do
  safe="${host//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/_}"
  outfile="$OUTDIR/${safe}.${timestamp}.txt"

  log "Tracing $host (mode=$MODE) -> $outfile"
  {
    echo "=== traceroute to $host @ $timestamp (UTC) ==="
    echo "Command: $TR_BIN ${opts[*]} $host"
    echo
    "$TR_BIN" "${opts[@]}" "$host"
  } |& tee "$outfile"
  echo
done

log "Done. Results in: $OUTDIR"
```

If you tell me whether you want UDP vs ICMP vs TCP (and which ports are allowed internally), I can tune the defaults for your environment.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# traceroute-capture-hops.sh
# Captures hop IPs for each target and writes:
#  - per-target raw traceroute output
#  - per-target hop IP list (unique, in first-seen order)
#  - combined CSV (target,hop,ip)
#
# Usage:
#   ./traceroute-capture-hops.sh                 # uses HOSTS below
#   ./traceroute-capture-hops.sh host1 host2     # uses args as targets
#
# Env:
#   OUTDIR=./traceroute-results
#   MAX_HOPS=30
#   WAIT_SEC=2
#   QUERIES=1
#   MODE=udp|icmp|tcp
#   TCP_PORT=443

HOSTS=(
  "dc01.internal"
  "files.internal"
  "git.internal"
  "db01.internal"
  "app01.internal"
)

OUTDIR="${OUTDIR:-./traceroute-results}"
MAX_HOPS="${MAX_HOPS:-30}"
WAIT_SEC="${WAIT_SEC:-2}"
QUERIES="${QUERIES:-1}"
MODE="${MODE:-udp}"          # udp (default), icmp (-I), tcp (-T)
TCP_PORT="${TCP_PORT:-443}"

timestamp="$(date -u +'%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')"
mkdir -p "$OUTDIR"

log() { printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +'%F %T UTC')" "$*" >&2; }

if ! command -v traceroute >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "ERROR: traceroute not found (install traceroute)."
  exit 127
fi

targets=("$@")
if [[ ${#targets[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  targets=("${HOSTS[@]}")
fi

opts=(-n -m "$MAX_HOPS" -w "$WAIT_SEC" -q "$QUERIES")
case "$MODE" in
  udp) : ;;
  icmp) opts+=(-I) ;;
  tcp)  opts+=(-T -p "$TCP_PORT") ;;
  *) log "ERROR: MODE must be udp|icmp|tcp (got: $MODE)"; exit 2 ;;
esac

csv="$OUTDIR/hops.${timestamp}.csv"
echo "target,hop,ip" >"$csv"

# Parse IPs from traceroute output (with -n, hops are numeric).
# Accept IPv4 and IPv6 tokens. Excludes '*' and duplicates per hop line.
extract_ips() {
  awk '
    # hop lines start with a number
    /^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]/ {
      hop=$1
      # gather IP-like tokens from the line
      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
        t=$i
        # Skip probe times like "1.234" / "ms"
        if (t=="*" || t=="ms") continue

        # IPv4
        if (t ~ /^([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}$/) {
          if (!(seen[hop SUBSEP t]++)) print hop, t
          continue
        }

        # IPv6 (simple heuristic: contains at least one colon)
        if (t ~ /^[0-9A-Fa-f:]+$/ && t ~ /:/) {
          if (!(seen[hop SUBSEP t]++)) print hop, t
          continue
        }
      }
    }
  '
}

for host in "${targets[@]}"; do
  safe="${host//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/_}"
  raw="$OUTDIR/${safe}.${timestamp}.traceroute.txt"
  ips="$OUTDIR/${safe}.${timestamp}.hop_ips.txt"

  log "Tracing $host (mode=$MODE)"
  traceroute "${opts[@]}" "$host" |& tee "$raw" > /dev/null

  # hop -> ip pairs (may include multiple IPs per hop if multipath)
  mapfile -t hop_ip_pairs < <(extract_ips <"$raw")

  # Write per-target hop IP list (unique IPs in first-seen order)
  : >"$ips"
  declare -A ip_seen=()
  for pair in "${hop_ip_pairs[@]}"; do
    hop="${pair%% *}"
    ip="${pair#* }"
    echo "$ip" >>"$ips"  # may have repeats; we'll uniq in-order below
  done
  awk '!seen[$0]++' "$ips" > "${ips}.tmp" && mv "${ips}.tmp" "$ips"

  # Append to combined CSV
  for pair in "${hop_ip_pairs[@]}"; do
    hop="${pair%% *}"
    ip="${pair#* }"
    echo "${host},${hop},${ip}" >>"$csv"
  done

  log "  raw: $raw"
  log "  ips: $ips"
done

log "Combined CSV: $csv"
```

Notes:
- This relies on `traceroute -n` so hops are already numeric (no DNS).
- If you want *exactly one IP per hop* (e.g., first IP only), say so and I’ll adjust the parser.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# traceroute-topology.sh
# Builds a simple text "topology map" from traceroute hops:
#  - topology.<timestamp>.txt : per-target path(s) as chains + edges
#  - topology.<timestamp>.edges.tsv : edge list (src -> dst) with counts
#
# Usage:
#   ./traceroute-topology.sh                 # uses HOSTS below
#   ./traceroute-topology.sh host1 host2     # uses args as targets
#
# Env:
#   OUTDIR=./traceroute-results
#   MAX_HOPS=30
#   WAIT_SEC=2
#   QUERIES=1
#   MODE=udp|icmp|tcp
#   TCP_PORT=443
#
# Notes:
# - Uses `traceroute -n` (no DNS) so IPs are parseable.
# - If multiple IPs appear on the same hop (ECMP), it will create edges for each.

HOSTS=(
  "dc01.internal"
  "files.internal"
  "git.internal"
  "db01.internal"
  "app01.internal"
)

OUTDIR="${OUTDIR:-./traceroute-results}"
MAX_HOPS="${MAX_HOPS:-30}"
WAIT_SEC="${WAIT_SEC:-2}"
QUERIES="${QUERIES:-1}"
MODE="${MODE:-udp}"
TCP_PORT="${TCP_PORT:-443}"

timestamp="$(date -u +'%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')"
mkdir -p "$OUTDIR"

log() { printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +'%F %T UTC')" "$*" >&2; }

if ! command -v traceroute >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "ERROR: traceroute not found."
  exit 127
fi

targets=("$@")
if [[ ${#targets[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  targets=("${HOSTS[@]}")
fi

opts=(-n -m "$MAX_HOPS" -w "$WAIT_SEC" -q "$QUERIES")
case "$MODE" in
  udp) : ;;
  icmp) opts+=(-I) ;;
  tcp)  opts+=(-T -p "$TCP_PORT") ;;
  *) log "ERROR: MODE must be udp|icmp|tcp (got: $MODE)"; exit 2 ;;
esac

topo_txt="$OUTDIR/topology.${timestamp}.txt"
edges_tsv="$OUTDIR/topology.${timestamp}.edges.tsv"
: >"$topo_txt"
: >"$edges_tsv"

# Output hop-indexed IPs from traceroute output (supports multi-IP per hop).
# Format: hop<TAB>ip
extract_hop_ips() {
  awk '
    /^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]/ {
      hop=$1
      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
        t=$i
        if (t=="*" || t=="ms") continue
        if (t ~ /^([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}$/) { print hop "\t" t; continue }
        if (t ~ /^[0-9A-Fa-f:]+$/ && t ~ /:/)      { print hop "\t" t; continue }
      }
    }
  '
}

# Deduplicate within a hop, preserve first-seen order
dedupe_per_hop() {
  awk -F'\t' '
    {
      hop=$1; ip=$2
      key=hop SUBSEP ip
      if (!seen[key]++) print
    }
  '
}

# Build edges from hop lists (multi-IP per hop creates a bipartite connection)
# Input: hop<TAB>ip (sorted by hop, grouped)
build_edges() {
  awk -F'\t' '
    function flush_prev(   i,j) {
      if (prev_n==0 || cur_n==0) return
      for (i=1; i<=prev_n; i++)
        for (j=1; j<=cur_n; j++)
          print prev[i] "\t" cur[j]
    }
    BEGIN { prev_hop=-1; prev_n=0; cur_hop=-1; cur_n=0 }
    {
      hop=$1; ip=$2
      if (cur_hop==-1) { cur_hop=hop }
      if (hop!=cur_hop) {
        # hop advanced: connect prev -> cur, then shift
        flush_prev()
        delete prev; prev_n=cur_n
        for (i=1; i<=cur_n; i++) prev[i]=cur[i]
        delete cur; cur_n=0
        cur_hop=hop
      }
      cur_n++; cur[cur_n]=ip
    }
    END {
      flush_prev()
    }
  '
}

# Count edges across all targets
declare -A edge_counts=()

for host in "${targets[@]}"; do
  safe="${host//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/_}"
  raw="$OUTDIR/${safe}.${timestamp}.traceroute.txt"

  log "Tracing $host (mode=$MODE)"
  traceroute "${opts[@]}" "$host" |& tee "$raw" > /dev/null

  # hop->ip pairs
  mapfile -t hopips < <(extract_hop_ips <"$raw" | dedupe_per_hop)

  {
    echo "=== Target: $host ==="
    echo "Raw: $raw"
    echo
    if ((${#hopips[@]}==0)); then
      echo "(no hop IPs parsed)"
      echo
      continue
    fi

    # Simple chain view: choose first IP per hop as the "main" path
    echo "Path (first IP per hop):"
    awk -F'\t' '
      { if (!seen[$1]++) { hops[++n]=$2 } }
      END {
        for (i=1; i<=n; i++) {
          printf "%s%s", hops[i], (i<n ? " -> " : "\n")
        }
      }
    ' < <(printf "%s\n" "${hopips[@]}")
    echo

    # Detailed per-hop (includes ECMP)
    echo "Hops (all IPs per hop):"
    awk -F'\t' '
      { hop=$1; ip=$2; a[hop]=a[hop] (a[hop]? " , ":"") ip; max=(hop>max?hop:max) }
      END { for (h=1; h<=max; h++) if (a[h]!="") printf "%2d: %s\n", h, a[h] }
    ' < <(printf "%s\n" "${hopips[@]}")
    echo
  } >>"$topo_txt"

  # Build and accumulate edges for this target
  mapfile -t edges < <(printf "%s\n" "${hopips[@]}" | sort -n -k1,1 | build_edges)
  for e in "${edges[@]}"; do
    [[ -n "$e" ]] || continue
    edge_counts["$e"]=$(( ${edge_counts["$e"]:-0} + 1 ))
  done
done

# Write global edge list + counts
{
  echo -e "src_ip\tdst_ip\tcount"
  for k in "${!edge_counts[@]}"; do
    src="${k%%$'\t'*}"
    dst="${k#*$'\t'}"
    echo -e "${src}\t${dst}\t${edge_counts[$k]}"
  done | sort -k3,3nr -k1,1 -k2,2
} >"$edges_tsv"

{
  echo "=== Combined topology edges (src -> dst with counts) ==="
  echo "Edges file: $edges_tsv"
  echo
  sed -n '1,200p' "$edges_tsv"
  echo
} >>"$topo_txt"

log "Topology map: $topo_txt"
log "Edges TSV:    $edges_tsv"
```

This stores a readable topology map in `traceroute-results/topology.<timestamp>.txt` plus an edge list in `topology.<timestamp>.edges.tsv`.
